content: If you suspect an overdose and the individual is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately by dialing 911. For non-emergency situations, contact a poison control center. In the United States, you can reach poison control at 1-800-222-1222, and in Canada, you can call 1-844-764-7669. If you are using this medication to treat diarrhea, it is important to drink plenty of water to reduce the risk of dehydration. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not freeze it, and avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in May 2024. Please note that this is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Side effects from this medication are rare. The most common side effects include darkening of the stool or tongue. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Persistent vomiting or diarrhea may lead to dehydration. Rarely, this medication can cause serious, potentially fatal bleeding in the stomach or intestines. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are also rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States or Canada, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking bismuth subsalicylate, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, aspirin, salicylates (e.g., salsalate), NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen, celecoxib), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Additionally, this medication may contain aspartame. It also contains a salicylate, which is similar to aspirin. Children and teenagers under 18 years old should not take this product if they have chickenpox, the flu, an undiagnosed illness, or have recently received a vaccine. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your doctor. This medication may harm an unborn baby and cause complications during labor or delivery. It is not recommended for use during pregnancy from 20 weeks until delivery. If your doctor determines that you need this medication between 20 and 30 weeks of pregnancy, use the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible time. Do not use this medication after 30 weeks of pregnancy. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk, but similar drugs are known to do so and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may increase the risk of bleeding when taken with other drugs that also increase bleeding risk. Carefully check the labels of all prescription and non-prescription medications, as many contain pain relievers or fever reducers (e.g., NSAIDs such as aspirin, ibuprofen, or naproxen) that are similar to this drug and may increase the risk of side effects. However, if your doctor has instructed you to take low-dose aspirin (usually 81-162 milligrams daily) to prevent heart attack or stroke, continue taking the aspirin unless directed otherwise. This medication may interfere with certain medical or laboratory tests, such as intestinal X-rays using contrast dye, potentially causing false test results. Always inform your healthcare provider about all medications you are taking before undergoing any tests.
